kernels.role_path: Local GEMM → Lamport-style flag/data all-reduce → output
kernels.synchronization_and_memory: Lamport flags establish shard visibility; ping-pong communication buffers cannot overlap the shard being consumed.

kernels.role_path: Local GEMM → LDX/STMC peer reduction path → output
kernels.synchronization_and_memory: Peer load/store completion gates communication-stage reuse; TMEM accumulator is distinct from distributed scratch.

kernels.role_path: Block-scaled GEMM → LDMC/XSTMC distributed reduction → scaled output
kernels.synchronization_and_memory: Scale metadata, TMEM result, and peer-reduction scratch overlap in time and therefore use separate allocations.

kernels.role_path: Local GEMM → reduce-scatter partitions the result → shard store
kernels.synchronization_and_memory: Each output shard releases after its peer reduction/store; collective scratch is separate from the TMEM accumulator.

kernels.role_path: Grouped scheduler loads problem descriptors → per-group TMA/tcgen05 → group output
kernels.synchronization_and_memory: Descriptor state persists across the group while operand stages and TMEM results retire per tile.

kernels.role_path: Grouped mixed-input conversion → tcgen05 → accumulator-scale epilogue
kernels.synchronization_and_memory: Per-group conversion metadata and accumulator scale are live with the result and use distinct storage.

kernels.role_path: Grouped descriptors → packed operand conversion/scaling → tcgen05 → D
kernels.synchronization_and_memory: Conversion metadata is group-specific; converted operand stages release after their tcgen05 consumer.

kernels.role_path: Packed mixed input plus scale/zero → producer conversion → tcgen05 → epilogue
kernels.synchronization_and_memory: Converted fragments and quantization metadata remain live through MMA and distinct from TMEM output.

kernels.role_path: Torch grouped-MoE descriptors → expert tile scheduler → tcgen05 expert GEMM
kernels.synchronization_and_memory: Expert routing metadata persists across assigned tiles; operand stages and expert result lifetimes are separate.

kernels.role_path: Scaled grouped-MoE descriptors → expert operands/scales → tcgen05 → routed output
kernels.synchronization_and_memory: Expert scale metadata tracks operand stages; routing, scale, and result storage remain distinct.

kernels.role_path: Separate TMA, MMA, and epilogue warps implement the first full FP16 GEMM pipeline
kernels.synchronization_and_memory: Mbarriers hand off A/B stages and TMEM result; TMA store releases the output stage.

kernels.role_path: CLC dynamically assigns persistent GEMM tiles to TMA/MMA/epilogue roles
kernels.synchronization_and_memory: CLC response and tile-complete signals are separate from A/B stage barriers and TMEM release.

kernels.role_path: Static persistent scheduler advances GEMM tiles through TMA, MMA, and epilogue roles
kernels.synchronization_and_memory: Tile advance waits for output retirement while K-stage reuse remains controlled by producer/consumer barriers.

kernels.role_path: Runtime preferred/fallback cluster shape selects multicast TMA and cooperative MMA
kernels.synchronization_and_memory: Cluster choice changes multicast participants; stage release waits for the chosen consumer set.

kernels.role_path: Initial plus rolling L2 prefetch runs ahead of TMA/MMA GEMM stages
kernels.synchronization_and_memory: Prefetch completion and A/B-stage readiness are separate events; their storage does not alias while live.

kernels.role_path: Programmatic dependent launch overlaps kernel launch sequencing with persistent GEMM
kernels.synchronization_and_memory: Dependent-launch completion is a launch-level event; in-kernel A/B and TMEM lifetimes retain normal barriers.

kernels.role_path: TMA load warp → SMEM transform warps → TMA store warp
kernels.synchronization_and_memory: A single input/output stage is transferred by mbarriers; TMEM is not used.

kernels.role_path: Persistent scheduler drives multistage TMA load → transform → TMA store
kernels.synchronization_and_memory: Independent load/store pipeline states recycle stage j only after both consumer and store completion; TMEM is unused.

kernels.role_path: CuTe extension stages A/B and block scales → tcgen05 → scaled epilogue
kernels.synchronization_and_memory: Operand and scale readiness are coupled; scale storage and TMEM accumulator remain separately addressable.

kernels.role_path: Two-SM cooperative TMA/tcgen05 mainloop → shared epilogue ownership
kernels.synchronization_and_memory: Both SM participants must release operand stages; distributed TMEM accumulator ownership converges before store.

kernels.role_path: CuTe Pipeline objects coordinate TMA producer, tcgen05 consumer, and epilogue
kernels.synchronization_and_memory: Pipeline states explicitly own acquire/commit/wait/release transitions for A/B and result storage.

kernels.role_path: Pointer-array scheduler selects per-batch A/B/C/D → tcgen05 GEMM
kernels.synchronization_and_memory: Pointer metadata persists for the tile while operand stages and TMEM result release independently.

kernels.role_path: CuTe extension TMA producer → tcgen05 MMA → TMEM epilogue
kernels.synchronization_and_memory: A/B mbarriers guard stage reuse; output staging remains distinct until the final store.

kernels.role_path: Q/K/V load producer → WGMMA QK/PV → online softmax → output
kernels.synchronization_and_memory: SM90 stores scores/P/output in registers and SMEM; K/V stage release follows WGMMA consumption.

kernels.role_path: TMA FP8 operands → WGMMA alternates two accumulator sets → epilogue
kernels.synchronization_and_memory: Two register accumulator sets overlap successive WGMMA groups and remain distinct until their epilogue turn.

kernels.role_path: Persistent FP8 TMA/WGMMA → fused GELU epilogue → D
kernels.synchronization_and_memory: Register accumulator stays live through GELU; epilogue scratch and operand SMEM stages remain distinct.

kernels.role_path: Persistent tile scheduler → TMA A/B → WGMMA → epilogue
kernels.synchronization_and_memory: A/B stages recycle per K tile; register accumulator persists across the K loop and output conversion.

kernels.role_path: TMA A/B producer → WGMMA consumer → epilogue store
kernels.synchronization_and_memory: Producer/consumer barriers recycle A/B stages; SM90 keeps the accumulator in registers, not TMEM.

kernels.role_path: Grouped problem scheduler → per-group TMA descriptors → WGMMA → group output
kernels.synchronization_and_memory: Problem metadata persists across each group while A/B stages and register results retire per tile.
